Secondary unknown: how F1 Fantasy prices Hadjar and Lawson returning to their original teams.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Universal consensus across all channels. ML projects 41.7 proj pts / 23.5 exp pts, ppm 2.07, LOW risk, DNF 0.05, pred P1→P1. ZachGP says 'without a doubt my guess for who's going to win this race is Kimi Antonelli' with fastest lap. Mercedes dominant in recent races and should suit Baku's long straights. No downside scenario beyond a crash.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lando Norris
captains.reason: ZachGP identifies Norris as the main alternative to Antonelli for 2x. McLaren brought a significant aero upgrade. ML projects 18.9 proj pts / 15.9 exp pts, ppm 1.38, MEDIUM risk. BoxBox predicts Antonelli-Norris-Verstappen podium. Lower ceiling than Antonelli but could pay off if Mercedes stumble. Channels favor Antonelli but Norris is the consensus backup captain.

buy.name: Alex Albon
buy.note: Williams bringing major upgrade package. Historical Baku success (2, 12, 13 pts last 3 years). Needs only -3 for min rise, 2 for max. Nearly 50% ownership in global top 500. All channels recommend as top escape from $3M assets.

buy.name: Franco Colapinto
buy.note: Averaging 11.1 pts/race, outperforming teammate Gasly recently. Back-to-back 13-14 pt scores. Longest active non-DNF streak. Needs only 2 pts for min rise. Strong budget builder at mid-price.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Cheapest reliable replacement for Perez/Stroll. Needs -3 for min rise, 2 for max. Solid floor — just finishes races consistently unlike $3M assets.

consider.name: Charles Leclerc
consider.note: IF engine penalty confirmed (10+ grid places), becomes a strong A-tier pick at lower price than Norris/Russell. FanAmp estimates ceiling ~P6 on a clean race (not Monza-level comeback). ML projects 22.3 proj pts / 17.3 exp pts WITHOUT penalty factored in. Even with penalty, FanAmp/ZachGP cite Spa precedent (Norris 40pts, Hadjar 38pts from back). Key risk: may run old engine, and Baku is P16/21 for overtakes.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Confirmed back at Racing Bulls. Scored 12, 2, 16 pts in last 3 Red Bull races. Pricing uncertainty is major concern — F1 Fantasy may reset his rolling average. If at Red Bull price (15.1M), needs 0 pts for min rise. At Racing Bulls price (9.7M), needs 27 pts for min rise. PolePosition calls him strong but in a pricing 'void' for 1-2 weeks.

consider.name: Oliver Bearman
consider.note: BoxBox highlights 4 pts for min rise, 9 for max. Haas brought upgrades recently. Under the radar but cheaper than Albon. ML not in top 8 but track could offer overtaking opportunities.

consider.name: Isack Hadjar
consider.note: ML projects 9.0 proj pts / 15.3 exp pts, value 1.06. Confirmed back at Red Bull. Same pricing uncertainty as Lawson — wait and see how F1 Fantasy handles his rolling average.

avoid: Lance Stroll — 10 DNFs, 7 in last 9 races, -122 fantasy pts on season. Budget decreasing asset.
Fernando Alonso — Also plagued by Aston Martin reliability. Budget decreasing asset.
Sergio Perez — 4 retirements in last 7 races. DNF machine at $3M floor.
Valtteri Bottas — Only scored >5 pts once all season (sprint weekend). Cadillac equally unreliable.
Yuki Tsunoda — 9.7M is too expensive for uncertainty of whether he races; better options elsewhere.
Carlos Sainz — Williams pre-upgrade, predicted low. Not worth the price.
Lewis Hamilton — Needs 77 pts for 0.3M rise, 55 pts for 0.1M. Budget decreasing. ML shows 16.7 proj pts, ppm 0.48 (lowest among A-tier). Ferrari not strong enough at Baku.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: Strong case if you need to escape multiple $3M assets (Stroll, Perez, Bottas) simultaneously. Triple header starts now — Baku then Malaysia/Bahrain then Singapore back-to-back-to-back with only one week break. If you're stuck with 2+ DNF-prone assets, this is a reasonable wildcard window to restructure to 3A/3.5A. However, some channels suggest saving for later triple headers.

chips.name: 3x Captain
chips.reason: Most managers have already used this chip (Monza/Zandvoort was the consensus window). If you still have it, Baku's overtaking limitations and lack of sprint make it less appealing than a sprint weekend or a track with more guaranteed overtakes.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No sprint weekend reduces ceiling. Better saved for a sprint triple-header or a weekend with clearer car hierarchy. ReinFantasy notes most top-10K managers have used high-value chips already.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Could be valuable if Leclerc penalty is confirmed late (after FP3 on Friday morning). The compressed Thursday-Friday-Saturday schedule means news breaks fast. Hold final fix in reserve for late-breaking penalty or setup changes.

watch_items: Leclerc engine penalty decision — Ferrari expected to announce after FP3 (Friday morning). If 10+ place penalty, he becomes a strong value pick but upside is capped vs Monza due to Baku's low overtake rate (P16/21 historically).
Williams upgrade package impact — James Vowles tempered expectations but new chassis for both cars. Watch FP1/FP2 Thursday to assess if Albon/Sainz gain meaningfully.
McLaren aero upgrade — significantly reduced sidepod air intake. BoxBox and ZachGP both flag this as potentially race-changing. Monitor practice pace closely.
Lawson & Hadjar pricing — F1 Fantasy has not communicated how rolling averages will be calculated for returning drivers. Could create pricing voids or opportunities.
Compressed schedule — FP1 and FP2 on Thursday, FP3 and Qualifying on Friday (deadline day), Race on Saturday. Sunday is Azerbaijan national remembrance day. Do NOT miss Friday qualifying deadline.
Battery deployment strategy on main straight — BoxBox notes the starting line proximity to Turn 1 makes energy management critical in qualifying. Could produce surprise grid positions.
George Russell penalty — reportedly deferred to COTA, NOT Baku. But monitor for any changes.
arc: Baku kicks off the first of three consecutive triple headers that will define the rest of the season. The key strategic shift is escaping $3M DNF-prone assets (Stroll, Perez, Bottas) and restructuring toward 3A/3.5A lineups with reliable mid-price drivers like Albon, Colapinto, and Hulkenberg. Budget is king at this stage — managers who started at 100M now have 130M+, and that gap will only widen. The Leclerc penalty situation and Williams upgrade are the two variables that could reshape the meta. After Baku, Malaysia/Bahrain follows immediately (likely another Mercedes-favored track), then Singapore (street circuit, potential safety cars). Managers should plan transfers across all three weekends now, conserving transfers for the grind phase where most chips have been spent and rank movement comes from consistent weekly optimization rather than chip-powered spikes.
